bugs.name: Enterococcus faecalis
bugs.disease: Urinary infection after cystoscopy, nitrite negative
bugs.micro: Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains; catalase-negative, non-hemolytic or alpha-hemolytic; blackens bile esculin agar, grows in 6.5% NaCl, PYR-positive; does not reduce nitrate; ampicillin inhibits but does not kill it
bugs.presentation: 70-year-old man 3 days after cystoscopy for an enlarged prostate: T 38.4 C, burning and urgency, mild suprapubic tenderness. Urine: leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite negative, 80 WBC/hpf, 10^5 CFU/mL of gram-positive cocci in chains; he took cephalexin last week.

bugs.name: Escherichia coli
bugs.disease: Burning, frequency and urgency without fever in a young woman
bugs.micro: Gram-negative enteric rod, motile; ferments lactose (pink on MacConkey, green metallic sheen on EMB); indole-positive, urease-negative, citrate-negative; type 1 fimbriae bind mannose on bladder cells; reduces nitrate to nitrite
bugs.presentation: 23-year-old woman: 2 days of burning on urination, going every 30 minutes, urgency and dull suprapubic ache, with visible blood in the urine at the end of the stream. No fever, no flank pain, no vaginal discharge; dipstick: leukocyte esterase and nitrite both positive.

bugs.name: Escherichia coli
bugs.disease: Fever with flank pain and white cell casts in the urine
bugs.micro: Gram-negative enteric rod, motile; ferments lactose (pink on MacConkey, green metallic sheen on EMB); indole-positive, urease-negative; P-pili bind digalactoside on renal tubular cells, letting it climb the ureter; alpha-hemolysin
bugs.presentation: 28-year-old woman with 2 days of burning and frequency, now T 39.3 C with rigors, nausea, vomiting and right-sided back pain; she winces when the right flank is struck. Urine: 100 WBC/hpf with casts made of white cells; nitrite positive; blood cultures drawn.

bugs.name: Escherichia coli
bugs.disease: Fever, chills and a boggy tender prostate at age 63
bugs.micro: Gram-negative enteric rod, motile; ferments lactose (pink on MacConkey, green metallic sheen on EMB); indole-positive and urease-negative; the usual isolate in men over 35, refluxing from the urethra into the prostatic ducts
bugs.presentation: 63-year-old man in the emergency department: 2 days of T 38.5 C, chills, frequency, burning, a hesitant stream and deep perineal pain. The prostate is warm, swollen and exquisitely tender on gentle rectal exam; urine culture grows 10^5 CFU/mL of a lactose fermenter.

bugs.name: Escherichia coli
bugs.disease: Fever without a source in a 3-month-old infant
bugs.micro: Gram-negative enteric rod, motile; ferments lactose (pink on MacConkey, green metallic sheen on EMB); indole-positive and urease-negative; the commonest isolate in childhood urinary infection; covered by a third-generation cephalosporin
bugs.presentation: 3-month-old girl: 2 days of T 39.4 C, poor feeding and irritability, with a normal ear, throat and chest exam and no rash. Catheter urine: leukocyte esterase positive, 50 WBC/hpf, 10^5 CFU/mL; ultrasound later shows urine refluxing up the right ureter.
